326dd3c.summary: Fires one ability of a card: loads trigger context, optionally pays spirit stones, picks the effect (all in order or one at random, optionally chance-gated), gathers targets, then dispatches on effect type to damage, heal, summon, draw, steal, buff or keyword actions queued on the battle manager. The decompiler merged parts of target gathering (GetTargets) into this body, so the tail is unreliable.
comments: Bail out (null check) if there is no battle manager; the pooled ability data is also needed
Fill the shared ability data with this trigger's context: card, played card, target, whose turn, priority
Spirit-stone trigger: the card using it pays the spirit stone cost before the effect resolves
Variable while-in-play trigger: mark the ability data so effects are tagged as extrinsic/variable
Plain while-in-play (aura) trigger: mark the ability data as while-in-play
Remember the damage info that caused this trigger so effects can read it
Continuous auras are silent; every other trigger plays its trait animation first
Record the activation in the match log for this player and trigger type
Normal case: every effect of the ability is played in order
Random ability choice (needs 2+ effects): pick a single effect index with the match RNG
Chance-based effect: values 1-99 take the dice-roll path at the end; anything else always fires
Resolve targets for the chosen effect; this is where an effect that passed its chance roll continues
Work out the repeat multiplier: count of targets, a trait total over targets, or just 1
Reset the list that collects cards created/drawn by this effect so later effects can reuse it
Clear the shared candidate-target list before resolving the second target set
Second target set (e.g. cards to buff/summon) is resolved and stored on the effect
Play the effect animation, except for a few follow-up/reference effect types that skip it
Final repeat count = effect's own multiplier times the value computed above
Giant dispatch on the effect type id; the decompiler flattened the switch into nested range checks
Tangled branch: effect type 0x32 adds a hand effect (buff to cards in hand), skipped for auras on other cards
Branch for a ranged-attack stat buff on this card; creates a fresh copy of the effect and fills its source info
Branch for stat-buff effects: one fresh copy of the buff effect is created and applied to every target
Aura buffs are not re-added if the target already carries the same extrinsic effect
After buffing, variable auras sweep units in play and strip extrinsic effects that no longer apply
Heal effect: amount comes from the effect's value criteria, then one or many characters are healed
Single target: heal one character; several targets: heal them all in one call
Types 0-11 group: draw a card for the caster, the opponent, or both depending on the target setting
Type 3 only logs a VFX-only effect; nothing else happens
Damage effect: amount from criteria, built into a damage record and dealt to every target at once
Sanity check: random damage must be randomised on resolution, otherwise reset to normal damage
Type 12: repeated random-target damage; hits on the same target are summed, then dealt together
Remember the target and its damage record; a repeat on the same target adds to its existing damage
Record pending damage on the target so later targeting sees it
Target was hit earlier in this loop: add this hit to its stored damage, or log an error if lists disagree
Deal all accumulated per-target damage in one networked/queued action
Type 15: damage all targets and then destroy the source card (e.g. self-destruct)
Mid-range types: cost change, summon units, transforms
Type 0x3c: change card Energy cost; the buff is scaled by the repeat count and queued
Summon-unit family of types: repeat for the repeat count, summoning every card the effect yields
Pick which side's minion row receives the summoned unit, then find a free slot
Slot choice depends on the effect's summon position: next to hero, target card, or this card
Look up the board position, then queue the summon with any attached buff
Special summon type that remembers the new unit on the acting card for later reference
Type 0x50: transform the acting card into the first card produced by the effect
Type 0x55: transform with an extra buff applied to the transformed card
Type 0x5a: transform every target into the chosen card
Type 100: create cards in hand for the caster, tracking them in the created-cards list
Type 0x6e: destroy every target unit, skipping invulnerable ones
Pick the destroy reason code: spell, own turn unit, or enemy unit; seems to feed destroy animation/keywords
Type 0x65: create copies of cards in hand, copying their effects onto the new cards
Types 0x88-0xa2: recall to hand (0x8c, 0x96), discard (0xa0), disappear (0xa2)
Type 0x78: jam each target unit
Type 0x82: stun each target unit
Type 0x87: shuffle the targets and stun up to the repeat count of them
Type 0xa5: discard whole hands of the affected player(s)
Type 0xaa: steal the targeted cards from hand
Type 0xaf: steal the targeted cards from the deck
Type 0xb4: steal the targeted minions
Types 0xb9 (steal the acting minion) and 0xbe (exchange self for a chosen minion)
No target found for exchangeSelfForMinion: log a warning, otherwise swap the minions
Type 200: steal a minion, or swap with a friendly one if the friendly criteria finds a candidate
Type 0xd2: copy each targeted unit from the cemetery
High effect types (0x15a and up): mostly trigger-granting effects and misc actions
Type 0x17c: remember the targets as this card's referenced cards
Types 0x177, 0x186, 400, 0x172: make targets trigger Sacrifice, Requiem, Courtesy, Relentless
Type 0x15e: remove each targeted card from the cemetery
Type 0x168: play the card picked in the selection; Oath cards also pay their Oath cost first
Oath card: pay the oath cost, fire the card, and repeat for each double-oath effect
Not an Oath card: simply trigger the chosen card's play ability
Clear the pending card now that it has been played
Types 0x19a-0x1e0: more keyword triggers (Codex, Regiment, Set card to top, Remnant transform)
Types 0x1b8, 0x1c2: Spirit Stone and Synapse triggers on each target
Types 0x1cc-0x1d4: Mob, Pray, Ambush, Uprising, Slay, Teleport triggers on each target
Type 0x1d6: open the show-cards window for the player
Type 0x1db: reset duty on each target
Type 0x1e0: highlight a bloodthirst card in the UI for the first target
Common tail: save this effect's results as the previous ability targets
Types below 0x123: attacks, resets, hand and board manipulations
Type 0xdc: reset each target's actions so it can act again
Types 0xe6-0xee: forced and scripted attacks (force attack, friendly force attack, redirect)
Type 0xee: scripted forced attack made by the source card; 0xf0 makes targets disappear
Type 0xfa: auto-play each targeted card from hand
Type 0x118 reveals orders then spends the enchantment; 0x122 makes the target miss
Type 0x104: copy targets to a list, then re-trigger each target's other ability per repeat
Type 0x10e: create cards in the deck for the repeat count and track them
Types 0x12c/0x12d: recall targets to deck (second variant flagged differently)
Type 0x140: queue a follow-up action after the current resolution
Type 0x136: display each targeted card from hand
Type 0x154: remove active enchantments on this card whose trigger matches
Type 0x159: remove enchantments the source ability itself placed on each target
Type 0x145: follow up only if the reference card is a valid target; otherwise play the animation and stop
Type 0x14a: draw until hands are equal, comparing opponent's and own hand sizes
Draw for the caster when the opponent has more cards (target 10 means self)
Positive difference: draw one card per card the opponent leads by
End of the effect switch; save drawn/created cards as previous ability targets
Chance roll path: roll 0-99 with match RNG, log it, and only run the effect if below the chance
Decompiler lost structure here: exception-handler leftovers; the code below is target gathering (GetTargets)
GetTargets body starts: clear the shared candidate list, then switch on the targeting type
Target type 0x14: just the acting card itself is the target
Target type 0x1e: the acting/triggering card; falls to the shared tail
Generic friendly/enemy flags are computed from whose card the ability is
Targets scaled by resource: one hero entry per spirit stone (0xa1) or faith (0xa2) point
Type 0xf5: one hero entry per secret played; type 0xaa: one per total Energy point
Hero-style targets: 0x5a a single card, 0x78 own hero, 0x82 opposing hero
Other targeting types: previous ability targets, filtered previous targets, cards in hand, deck, cemetery
Special cases: 200 uses stored cards, 0xc9 uses stored cards still in play, 0xe6 highest health warlord
Collect candidate lists from hand, deck, cemetery, units in play, or adjacent units based on type
Filter pass: remove every candidate that fails the ability's criteria, walking from the end
Optional extra filter: keep only candidates created by the same enchantment
Limit results: if more candidates than allowed, choose by ordering mode (lowest, highest, random, etc.)
Mode 5 takes from the end of the list, mode 7 from the start; other modes pick random targets
Default selection: pick the requested number of random targets, removing each from the pool
Type 0xc9: stored cards that are still in play become targets
Type 0xe6 picks the highest-health warlord, falling back to both heroes; 0xf0 lowest-health unit
Type 0xa0: one hero entry per unused Energy point on each affected side
Debug log of how many targets were found for current Energy
Remaining target types: 0xbe cards played, 0xb4 random card from the full collection, 0xdc
Type 0xb4: build a pool of creatable cards from the whole collection meeting the criteria
Cards flagged as not randomly creatable or hidden are left out
One special card id also drops cards with single-use mutations
Shared tail for the triggering-card target types
Decompiler fragment: tail of the follow-up/enchantment loops, adding missing extrinsic effects
Cleanup: some effect types finish by saving targets as previous ability targets
Decompiler fragment: loop that re-triggers other cards' abilities once per repeat
